title: Lionel Messi’s Landmark Argentina Moments in Pictures
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath12:30 PM EDTIt’s been some ride. / Jabin Botsford/The Washington Post via Getty ImagesLionel Messi’s 21-year international career has reached its end.

The iconic Estadio Monunmental in Buenos Aires will play host to a piece of soccer history as the 39-year-old superstar signs off with his 208th and final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin on Tuesday.
There will be fireworks and waterworks in equal measure at the big farewell for one of Argentina and the world’s greatest-ever players.
From 2005 to 2026, here’s a look back at the Argentina moments that made Messi, from the significant and the spectacular. It’s been some ride.

Messi received a red card on his Argentina debut. / Michael Mayhew/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty ImagesIn a quirk of fate, a floppy-haired, 18-year-old Messi makes his senior Argentina debut against Hungary—the very same opponent Diego Maradona had faced in his first appearance for the national team back in 1977.

The match is not exactly the anointing of Maradona’s successor many had anticipated. Messi comes on after 63 minutes and was sent off by German referee Markus Merk on 65, having been judged to have thrown an elbow at defender Vilmos Vanczak (above) in a tussle for the ball.

Messi soon bounced back from his sending off. / ATTILA KISBENEDEK / AFP via Getty ImagesThe BBC’s South American soccer expert Tim Vickery calls the controversial sending off a “crime against football.”
Messi scored the sixth against Serbia & Montenegro. /  Tony Marshall - PA Images via Getty ImagesMessi is not yet 19 when he scores his first World Cup goal.
Argentina confirmed its spot in the knockout stages with an emphatic 6–0 win over Serbia & Montenegro in Gelsenkirchen, with Messi making his tournament debut off the bench.

The teenager only had 15 minutes of the second half to make an impact but set up Hernán Crespo for the fourth, before adding the sixth himself—darting into space at the edge of the box and striking neatly across goal, with what would soon become a trademark finish.

Messi soon became the main man for Argentina. /  MIGUEL ROJO/AFP via Getty Images)AFP via Getty ImagesGrizzled veteran Juan Sebastián Verón is reduced to a giddy fanboy as Messi made it 2–0 in the Copa América semifinal against Mexico.

Messi—with shoulder-length hair and wearing the number 18 on his back—loops one over Oswaldo Sánchez from the edge of the 18-yard box. It is as aesthetically pleasing a goal as you are ever likely to see and one which announced Messi as the superstar everyone in Argentina and Barcelona told the world he would be.

Diego Maradona link-up with Lionel Messi did not bring success. /  DANIEL GARCIA / AFP via Getty ImagesThe attempt to pair with Messi and Maradona as player and manager proved a flawed experiment as Argentina is eliminated at the 2010 World Cup quarterfinal having been torn to pieces by Germany in a 4–0 defeat.

Having played lighter as the exciting, up-and-coming prospect at previous tournaments, 2010 was the first time Messi—by now a Champions League and Ballon d’Or winner—felt the crushing weight expectation to replicate the heroics of the man in the dugout. He ended the 2010 tournament with no goals in five games.

Messi scored his first international hat-trick against Brazil. / Tim Clayton/Corbis via Getty ImagesMetLife Stadium was the venue for Messi’s first-ever international hat trick, with more than 80,000 watching live as the superstar powered Argentina to an all-time classic of a 4–3 friendly win against Brazil—a clash that was billed as Messi vs. Neymar in the buildup.

Close but not close enough. /  Chengdu Economic Daily/VCG via Getty ImagesMessi glumly accepted the Golden Ball as the 2014 World Cup’s best player moments after Argentina fell to an extra-time defeat to Germany in the final in Rio de Janeiro. Meanwhile, photos are snapped of the forward looking on at the trophy he really wanted.
With the forward in his peak years and three tournaments in, questions are beginning to be asked about how many more chances he would get at soccer’s grand prize.

The 2014 World Cup final starts a run of painful final defeats. / ALFREDO ESTRELLA/AFP via Getty ImagesThe World Cup final loss triggers a run of painful final defeats, with Messi’s Argentina falling short in back-to-back Copa América tournaments—both times on penalties, both times to Chile.
In the 2016 Centenario tournament held in the United States, Messi scored five times but missed the opening penalty of the shootout the final.

Messi’s first retirement triggered an outpouring of national grief. /  Amilcar Orfali/LatinContent via Getty ImagesMessi, then 29, retires from Argentina duty following the heartbreak, saying: “For me, the national team is over. I've done all I can. It hurts not to be a champion.”
